nativeConsult.question: For an isolated get_feedback answering session seeded from a genuinely live expert transcript, what bounded production evidence distinguishes legitimate source continuation from an answering child mutating the source's canonical claims or waking the source? We need to verify the source transcript prefix and native identity, and attribute consult-window tool effects. Recommend the smallest concrete verification method for the existing consult/session-port lifecycle, including how to handle mutate-then-revert, plan-only claims and system-direct effects without asserting universal same-UID filesystem immutability.
nativeConsult.tried: Read the stable live JSONL descriptor/prefix reader, consult dispatch exact source/native binding, native consult boundary capture and the real transport actor guard. Existing clean committed actor controls pass and the header-first counterexample is caught; conventional dispatch source/bypass controls also pass. A separate live Claude-source request retained only ended or wrong-backend sources and closed honestly unavailable. The router now constrains the registered source population before transcript, subject and menu bounds; exact current staging source bytes match the committed repair. This fresh trial changes the source/target backend cell and preserves floors. Before dispatch we capture raw canonical assignments and plan_item_claims for all registered not-ended Codex source owners in one read transaction.
nativeConsult.observed: Matching before/after canonical claims cannot exclude ABA mutation or distinguish legitimate work by a later source continuation from child/system effects. The native boundary records completeBytes, source SHA and descriptor identity plus canonical held work-items, but explicitly excludes plan-only claims, wakes and actor history. The transport actor guard rejects a child native session spoofing a valid source owner; its conventional fixture proof does not establish production isolation. A substantive source-grounded answer will inform the remaining bounded production verification, not itself count as full matrix or shipment acceptance.
nativeConsult.decision_at_stake: Choose the minimal actor-bound dispatch-window verification and source-prefix/claim observation to retain in the maintained native consult acceptance evidence. Decide which observed effects can be attributed and which must remain unknown, while allowing independent source continuation and keeping optional system-quality reporting optional.
